profiles.heading: Profiles
profiles.note: Every profile of every kind — this realm's default, a default inherited from the default realm or still on the built-in defaults, and every named profile. Who names a named profile is on that kind's tab. The list is paged like every list in this console.
profiles.json: The same over JSON is /admin/policies?format=json and GET /admin-api/policies; the actions on this page are
lead: A policy here is a rule this realm holds a credential to. Each kind is a SEPARATE policy with its own entry in its own container and its own tab, and each has a profile — default — which applies to every person in this realm. Every kind may also keep named profiles. A named profile lists nobody: an application, a group or a person names it, and where several apply the one with the lowest precedence does.
notXacml: . This is not the XACML policy repository:
notXacmlEnd: holds documents a PDP evaluates, in ou=policies.
authn.heading: Authentication policy — the default profile
authn.lead: Which ways of signing in this realm accepts as a FIRST factor and as a SECOND, and when a second factor is required. Asked at every sign-in door, in both modes: this policy decides what the sign-in screen offers, not whether a credential is checked.
authn.noMail: This realm cannot send mail, so the two email mechanisms are drawn disabled below and are never offered. Configure a transport on
authn.fromRealm: This realm's own profile is stored at {dn}. Removing it puts this realm back to the default realm's profile, or to the built-in defaults where the default realm has none.
authn.fromDefaultRealm: This realm has no profile of its own, and follows the default realm's ({dn}). Saving this form writes this realm's own, which overrides it here and nowhere else.
authn.builtIn: Nothing is stored, so the built-in defaults are in force. Saving this form writes cn=default under ou=authnPolicies. Saved in the DEFAULT realm, it is the policy of every realm that has none of its own.
authn.checked: Every field is checked before anything is written. At least one mechanism must be accepted as a first factor, and if a second factor is required of everybody at least one must be accepted as a second. A person who HOLDS a second factor is asked for it whatever this says: there is no setting that skips a held factor.
authn.now: What this realm accepts, right now
authn.dash: A dash is a role the mechanism cannot have: an authenticator app or a recovery code is never a first factor, and a certificate, a Kerberos ticket, a wallet or a federation partner is never asked for second.
authnNamed.heading: Named authentication policies
authnNamed.lead: An application names the authentication policy it follows (appAuthnPolicy on its Configuration tab), and a group may name one for its members (stsAuthnPolicy on the group's page). Where several are named for one sign-in, the one with the lowest precedence applies; where none is, or only default, this realm's policy above applies as it is. A named policy holds only two lists: the first-factor mechanisms and the second factors a sign-in it applies to allows. Nothing ticked allows every one the realm allows. A policy is this realm's own, and cannot be deleted while an application or a group names it.
authnNamed.name: Name
authnNamed.inUse: An application or a group names this policy; point it at another first.
authnNamed.empty: This realm has no named authentication policy.
named.name: Name
named.heading: Named profiles
named.noteRanked: A named profile lists nobody. It applies, instead of the default, where an application, a group or a person names it, and where several match, the one with the lowest precedence applies. A realm's named profiles are its own and are not inherited.
named.noteUnranked: A named profile lists nobody. It applies, instead of the default, where an application, a group or a person names it. Nothing is ranked. A realm's named profiles are its own and are not inherited.
named.noteReferenced: A named profile lists nobody. It applies, instead of the default, where an application, a group or a person names it — whichever of those this kind has — and where several apply, the one with the lowest precedence does. A realm's named profiles are its own and are not inherited.
clients.heading: Clients a registration offers no ML-DSA, learned
clients.note: A client is a browser and a system, by family and major version, as the passkey ceremony rows name it. While webauthn.clientLearning is on, a client from which {threshold} different people's registrations asked for ML-DSA and failed with NotSupportedError within {hours} hours, and none succeeded, is learned: its registrations offer no ML-DSA where a classical passkey is allowed. Clearing it, or a registration from it that succeeds, offers it ML-DSA again. The configured rules are each profile's clientRules row.
clients.learningOff: Learning is off in this realm (webauthn.clientLearning): nothing is counted, and the clients listed are not applied.
clients.none: No client has been counted in this realm.
clients.failures: People who failed, in the window
password.heading: Password policy — the default profile
password.lead: What a password set in this realm must look like. It is stored as {dn}, in the shape of draft-behera-ldap-password-policy (the schema OpenLDAP's ppolicy overlay reads), so an ldapsearch finds it and an ldapmodify changes it.
password.stored: This profile is stored at {dn}. Saving replaces it; removing it deletes it, after which the built-in defaults below are in force.
password.builtIn: Nothing is stored yet, so the built-in defaults are in force. Saving this form writes cn=default under ou=passwordPolicies in this realm's directory. A realm created later starts with the same built-in defaults rather than a copy of this one — the profile is not seeded, so it cannot be missing from a realm nobody seeded.
password.checked: Every field is checked before anything is written, and two rules relate fields to each other: a generated password must be at least the minimum length, and at least twice the symbol count plus two — a generator asked for more symbols than that would be drawing for a very long time. A change applies to the NEXT password set in this realm; nothing already stored is re-checked, because a stored password is a hash and there is nothing left to check it against.
password.rulesHeading: What a password must be, right now
password.rules2: and the activation page print them to the person choosing a password, so the page they read and the rule this service applies are one sentence.
password.doors: Every door that sets a password ends in one function in common/credentials.ts, which is what makes the list below complete rather than a list somebody remembered.
password.historyHeading: The history, and what it costs
password.history: A remembered password is the hash it was already stored as, moved into pwdHistory on the person's own entry when the next one replaces it — no new hash is made, and the password itself is never kept. Checking a new password costs one hash comparison per remembered one, about 70ms each on this thread, so a history of {history} is up to {ms}ms at a password change. A generated password skips the comparison, because nothing drawn at random is a previous password. pwdHistory and pwdChangedTime are maintained by this service and an LDAP modify naming either is refused in product mode.
password.generator1: New users created from the console or /admin-api get a generated password by default, shown or returned ONCE. It is drawn by
password.generatorUntil: , which silently end or change a string pasted into a shell or a JSON body), and it draws until
password.schema: This directory is schemaless, so a container of entries carrying invented attributes says what they mean here. The pwd* names are draft-behera-ldap-password-policy's; the stsPwd* ones are this service's own, because the draft delegates composition rules to the server and defines none.

attributes.heading: Attribute policy — the default profile
attributes.lead: The attributes every person in this realm must hold a value of, and the realm's own custom attributes. uid, cn and sn are always required; tick any other attribute a person here may be given. A person created without a cn is given one made of their given name and surname. A person created before an attribute was required keeps every other door, and nobody's sign-in is refused for it.
attributes.enforced: ENFORCED. This realm is in product mode, so every door that creates a person — this console, /admin-api, SCIM, an LDAP add, a federated first sign-in, the bulk import — refuses one without a required attribute, and an edit may not take one away.
attributes.notEnforced: NOT ENFORCED. This realm is in development mode, where a person may be created with no more than a username. The list is still stored and drawn. Switch the realm with global.mode on
attributes.fromRealm: This realm's own profile is stored at {dn}. Removing it puts this realm back to the default realm's profile, or to the built-in default where the default realm has none.
attributes.fromDefaultRealm: This realm has no profile of its own, and follows the default realm's ({dn}). Saving this form writes this realm's own, which overrides it here and nowhere else.
attributes.builtIn: Nothing is stored, so the built-in default is in force: givenName, sn and mail. Saving this form writes cn=default under ou=attributePolicies. Saved in the DEFAULT realm, it is the policy of every realm that has none of its own.
attributes.tableLabel: Every attribute a person in this realm may be given, and whether it is required
attributes.label: Label
attributes.missingAsk: Count the people who lack a required attribute
attributes.missingCount: {n} people in this realm lack a value of an attribute their own profile requires.
attributes.missingNotCounted: This realm's directory is held in the store, so the people who lack a required attribute are not counted here.
attributes.missingFilter: Under ou=users, the LDAP filter that finds those lacking an attribute the default profile requires is
attributes.namedLead: A named profile applies, instead of the default, to a person who names it through stsAttributePolicy on their own entry, and to a member of a group that names it the same way; where several apply, the one with the lowest precedence does. A reference to a profile this realm does not hold selects nothing. A realm's named profiles are its own and are not inherited.
attributes.customLead: Attributes this realm adds to what a person may be given: each is then editable on a person's page, settable when a person is created, checked against its syntax, and may be required above. They are this realm's own and are not inherited from the default realm. A custom attribute cannot be removed while anybody holds a value of it, or while any of this realm's profiles requires it. At most {max}.
attributes.noCustom: This realm defines no custom attribute.
attributes.portalVisible: Show it to the person on the portal
attributes.portalEditable: Let the person change it on the portal
attributes.portalNote: Both off by default. Letting the person change it also shows it.
attributes.changeFixed: The syntax and whether it holds several values cannot be changed.
securityOnly: Only a Security Administrator may save, reset or act on a policy here, or name one on an application, group or person. You can read every policy; a change is refused.
transfer.heading: Export and import
transfer.lead: Export writes every profile this realm stores, on every tab of this page, into one JSON document signed under this realm's Policy Export Signing CA, with the signer's whole certificate chain inside it. Import writes such a document into this realm through each kind's own Save. The algorithm is the setting pki.policyExportAlgorithm.
transfer.importNote: Paste an export below. Check the signer first: its chain is validated in full, and another realm's export is never imported until you are asked whether to trust its signer.
transfer.origin.own: Signed by this realm's own Policy Export Signing CA. It is trusted.
transfer.origin.trusted: Signed by another realm whose chain this realm's signer truststore already holds for policy imports. It is trusted.
transfer.origin.foreign: Signed by another realm, {realm}, whose chain this realm does not trust yet.
transfer.chain: The signer's chain, the signing certificate first
transfer.subject: Subject
transfer.verdictOk: The chain passed full PKI validation: validity, key usage, the path and revocation of every certificate.
transfer.verdictRefused: The chain was refused by PKI validation, so nothing can be imported.
transfer.question: Trust this signer for policy imports in this realm? Yes adds the three certificate authorities above to this realm's signer truststore, for policy imports and nothing else, and imports the document. The Issuing CA's fingerprint is {fingerprint}.
transfer.trustAndImport: Yes: trust this chain and import
transfer.selectNote: Tick the policies to export, or tick none to export every policy this realm stores. Each policy also has an Export button of its own on the All profiles tab.
transfer.importSelectNote: Untick a policy to leave it out of the import. With none ticked, every policy in the export is imported.
transfer.exportOneTip: Download the signed export of {kind} {name} alone.
transfer.view.paranoid: Full paranoid validation of an export's signer (pki.paranoidPolicySigner)
transfer.view.noIssuingCa: This realm has no Policy Export Signing CA yet. The first export builds it.
transfer.view.fingerprintNote: An administrator in another realm names this fingerprint to trust this realm's exports.
transfer.view.noneTrusted: This realm trusts no other realm's policy exports.
